title: Tusi couple first presented
summary: In late October 1245, in the town of Tun (today Firdaws) in southern Khurasan, Nasir al-Din al-Tusi completed a Persian appendix to his Mu'iniyya treatise that first presented the device now called the Tusi couple: two linked circles, one twice the size of the other, that make a point oscillate along a straight line. A second version appeared in his Almagest recension of 13 February 1247, and the fullest account in his Tadhkira of 1261, which first appeared while he directed the Maragha observatory.

uncertainty.note: Start is the completion date of the Hall-i mushkilat-i Mu'iniyya (first part of Jumada II 643 AH = late October 1245, per Ragep). The Tahrir al-Majisti (second version) was completed 13 February 1247 and the Tadhkira first appeared in 1261; end is the Tadhkira.

where.historical_name: Tun, in Quhistan, southern Khurasan, under the Ismaili rulers of Quhistan

importance.justification: Tusi's device let planetary models keep uniform circular motion at Ptolemaic accuracy, and it later influenced Islamic and European astronomers (Biographical Encyclopedia of Astronomers).

reviewer_note: Least sure of the id: the queue id says 1247, but Ragep dates the first presentation to late October 1245 (Hall-i mushkilat-i Mu'iniyya, written at Tun); 1247 is the second version in the Almagest recension. The queue brief said Maragheh, but the Maragha observatory only appears for the 1261 Tadhkira, so the pin is Tun (Ragep: today called Firdaws, about 80 km WNW of Qa'in) at the GeoNames Ferdows point; the garden Bagh Barakah is not located.
